# Independent Mac Hancom editing captures

This set covers five of the six diagnostic recipes: body paragraph spacing, an empty table cell, mixed body text, mixed cell text and cell paragraph spacing. Unlike the earlier import/export captures, these edits were performed in Hancom from byte-verified copies of the same pre-edit sources used by Rau.

The [capture record](capture.json) pins the source, both independently edited HWPX files and the Hancom PDF. `edited.hwpx` is Hancom's output. `rau-edited.hwpx` is Rau's output. `hancom-independent.pdf` is the PDF exported after the observed Hancom edits. Each complete page was rendered with Poppler and visually inspected, at 96 DPI for the first four cases and scale-to 1400 for cell paragraph spacing.

The body operations were an inline 180 × 90 pt picture in the empty second paragraph, 6 pt before, 3 pt after and 160 percent line spacing. Hancom's dialog showed the corresponding 63.50 × 31.75 mm image size. The cell operation inserted the same image inline in the first paragraph of cell A1, with no text or formatting changes. Saved XML confirms its dimensions and ownership. Differences in picture attributes, stored table height and producer metadata remain recorded, not silently edited away.

The mixed-body operation inserted the same inline image at Unicode offset 10, between `그림 앞의 글입니다` and the first period. The original text remains intact, with 0 pt before/after and 160 percent line spacing. Saved XML verifies the insertion offset, image bytes, dimensions and inline setting. Its complete PDF page was visually inspected.

The mixed-cell operation inserted the image at the same Unicode offset in A1, without changing its text or formatting. Saved XML verifies ownership, dimensions, exact text offset, cell geometry and paragraph properties. Hancom stores overall table height 15364 HU while Rau stores 2564 HU. These values remain untouched; actual cell bounds are compared with the native PDF. The complete exported page was visually inspected.

The cell-spacing operation inserted the same image at the beginning of A1, then applied 6 pt above and 3 pt below its paragraph with 160 percent line spacing. Saved XML verifies that only A1 received this formatting and all source text remains unchanged. An initial accessibility field readback appeared successful but did not change the saved properties; that attempt was rejected. Actual keyboard entry and a subsequent XML check verified the final operation.

All five cases pass at the unchanged 0.5 pt bound. See the [five-case parallel-edit report](five-case-word-spacing-parallel-comparison.json) and [five-case Hancom-import report](five-case-word-spacing-import-comparison.json). The new case checks all 55 visible glyph origins, image bounds and all four cell rectangles. Its maximum horizontal glyph error is 0.127 pt, baseline error 0.100 pt, image error 0.011 pt and cell-boundary error 0.120 pt. Each case retains identical live layout through three save/reopen cycles in both modes.

The initial five-case [parallel](five-case-initial-parallel-comparison.json) and [import](five-case-initial-import-comparison.json) reports failed on the second character of `그림` beside the image, with 1.774 pt horizontal error despite matching image, lines and cells. Justification counted the wrapped word's trailing space in its width and character count, compressing the visible letters. Excluding trailing spaces from this calculation reduces that character's error to 0.086 pt. The shared body/cell calculation has a failing-before, passing-after unit test, with and without reserved inline-object width. No captured file or tolerance changed.

The earlier four cases passed in the [four-case parallel-edit report](four-case-fractional-parallel-comparison.json) and [four-case Hancom-import report](four-case-fractional-import-comparison.json). Both mixed-text cases gate all 55 visible glyph origins. Maximum horizontal error is below 0.143 pt for mixed body text and 0.097 pt for mixed cell text. Baseline errors stay below 0.100 pt, and image errors stay below 0.041 pt. Every table cell matches native PDF border geometry within 0.120 pt. All cases retain identical live layout through three save/reopen cycles in both modes.

The initial four-case [parallel](four-case-initial-parallel-comparison.json) and [import](four-case-initial-import-comparison.json) reports failed the mixed-cell glyph gate by up to 0.556 pt. The native renderer rounded run widths and trailing spaces separately, adding excess justification spacing across words. The Mac policy now retains fractional widths, matching its glyph positions and the existing WASM measurer. Windows reference rounding is unchanged. No captured input, PDF or tolerance changed.

The initial [glyph-aware parallel report](three-case-initial-glyph-parallel-comparison.json) and [import report](three-case-initial-glyph-import-comparison.json) correctly failed the mixed-body case. Its last period drifted by 0.580 pt despite passing image placement and line-start checks. Correcting HCR Batang's Mac Hangul advance from 9.70 to the observed 9.72 pt reduced the drift without changing any captured file or tolerance. The PDF's text transform uses a 0.12 pt device grid and an 83-unit em at nominal 10 pt. Consecutive Hangul glyphs advance about 81 device units. The same advance is present in the body-spacing and mixed-cell captures. This correction does not establish Latin shaping or other font/size parity.

The remaining independent recipe is a width-fitted cell image. These cases do not establish full formatting parity. Whitespace origins, glyph outlines and individual glyph positions outside the three text-bearing body/cell image cases are not gated. Keep captured files and historical reports immutable. The earlier [three-case parallel](three-case-hangul-grid-parallel-comparison.json), [three-case import](three-case-hangul-grid-import-comparison.json), [two-case parallel](two-case-parallel-comparison.json), [two-case import](two-case-import-comparison.json), body-only [parallel](initial-parallel-comparison.json) and [import](initial-import-comparison.json) reports remain historical evidence.

Use the [independent comparison commands](../../../../tools/editing_parity/README.md#independent-edit-comparison) to create new evidence without overwriting these initial reports.
